newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives deny planning tax privatisation.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives deny planning tax privatisation.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major's beleagured government, hunting for policies to win an upcoming election, is not planning to privatise the country's tax authorities, a senior minister said on Tuesday.

Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell said a pre-election cabinet brainstorming session led by Major on Monday drew up plans to continue the reform drive of the Conservative government to improve efficiency and maximise savings. The election is due by May at the latest.
But he dismissed newspaper reports of a wholesale privatisation of the tax service.

"It doesn't mean privatising the government department of the Inland Revenue...There is no proposal to privatise a government department in that sense," said Dorrell, who was responsible for the tax service when he was a treasury minister.
The Guardian said the government was drawing up privatisation plans involving the sale of 450 tax offices and the introduction of private contractors to assess tax returns.

The newspaper report was one of a series speculating on the conclusions of the brainstorming session at the prime minister's country residence, which was designed to pull together key ideas for the crucial election manifesto.
Polls put the government well behind the opposition Labour party with time ticking away to the election.
Dorrell said contractors had for some time been involved in some aspects of the Inland Revenue's work but private companies would not see individual tax returns.

"There is a contract to have the computer services managed by the...world's largest information-handling company in order to achieve savings, but of course safeguarding the confidentiality commitment of the Inland Revenue," he said.
"Confidentiality is the bedrock of the work of the Inland Revenue, but what we also need to do is ensure that we deliver the service efficiently."
